newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firmer, poised for steady growth.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firmer, poised for steady growth.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mostly firmer in active trade on Friday and market participants said liquid issues were poised for a steady growth in the days ahead.
"Prices will rise a bit every day," said Davor Relja, an analyst at Faktor brokerage, attributing the growth partly to a relatively scarce supply.
Volume almost doubled to 33,152 shares on Friday and turnover also rose to 12.5 from 7.6 million kuna.
Seven of the 12 active issues rose, four fell and one remained flat as the fully listed Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva in London pulled the market up.
Biggest gainer Zagrebacka Banka rose 110 kuna to hit a new high of 1,870 kuna, after peaking at 1,900 earlier in the session. It sold only 129 shares.
Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs), trading at London's Seaq, rose to $33.5 by mid-afternoon, up from $31.5.
The bank's E-series preference stock gained 50 kuna to 1,000, with 2,335 shares sold.
Pliva inched up three kuna to 513 on volume of 889 shares. Its GDRS rose to $17.435 from Thursday's $17.185 on the London Stock Exchange.
Food processor Podravka accounted for most of the day's trading, edging up 13 kuna to 318 on volume of 26,863 shares.
"It is foreign investors who are mostly buying Podravka at the moment," Relja said.
He added their interest could be ascribed to a rumoured deal on investment with the European Bank for reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Analysts also expect Podravka to show better results for 1996, recovering from a loss in the previous year.
Foreign buyers were said to be increasingly interested in hotel shares to add to Zagrebacka and Pliva.

Hotelier Laguna rose 50 kuna to 1,300 on volume of 316 shares, while Jadranturist added five kuna to 306, selling 1,880 units. Istraturist edged down six kuna to 190 and Arenaturist was flat at 160 kuna.
Privatisation candidate Adriatic pipeline Janaf was also among gainers, rising 50 kuna to 5,550, selling only 11 shares.
Dubrovnik shipper Atlantska Plovidba was top decliner, losing 78 kuna to 102 and selling 115 shares in a first deal since November. Cable maker Elka lost five kuna to 190.
Confectioner Kras inched down five kuna to 445, with 314 shares changing hands.
